name: Soft Landing
description: Fictional biomaterials seed pitch for art logistics.

slides.title: Soft Landing
items: Grown-to-fit packaging for touring ceramics
Illustrative seed pitch

slides.title: A new crate at every stop
items: When an exhibition travels, a different crew often packs the same object again. The first crew’s hand-cut foam and handwritten notes rarely tell the next handler exactly where the weight should rest.
A handle is easy to see. The place where it can safely carry weight is harder to communicate.
We sell the repeatable fit to the art shipper who has to deliver the next leg.

slides.title: Grow the negative space
items: A handler approves the contact points on a digital model. Two complementary molds turn that approval into a pair of fitted cushions.
We grow a mycelium-bound fiber composite in the molds, dry the parts and check their dimensions. Each new pair uses the approved geometry.

slides.title: A packer can read the fit
items: The rim and handles sit inside clearance pockets. The two inserts meet at the body, where the registrar approved support.
The packer checks the orientation mark, closes the lid and records the insert revision on the loan paperwork. A replacement can be ordered against that revision.

slides.title: The second order changes the economics
items: One-time fit and tooling fee per approved object. It covers the model review, first mold and registrar sign-off.
Price per replacement pair. At $42 of direct material, labor and drying cost, one pair contributes $54 before overhead and freight.

slides.title: Begin with repeat shippers
items: 40 art shippers
Assume each handles 25 suitable object families per year. At one new fit and four paid pairs per family, annual sales would be $864,000 across the initial group.
The sales list starts with shippers that service recurring ceramics exhibitions. Registrars approve object contact. The shipper owns the purchasing decision.

slides.title: A trial on the packing bench
items: Packing time per object • illustrative rehearsal
Across three object types, the modeled average falls from 30 to 15 minutes. Repeat packers already have an approved fit sheet for the molded system.
Before live loans, test vibration, drop response and material compatibility with sacrificial objects. Faster packing alone does not qualify an insert.

slides.title: What the shipper can buy today
items: Foam cut on site
Fast to source and easy to adjust. Each new crew has to reproduce the original support by hand.
A custom rigid case
A good choice for an object that travels in the same case for years. Storage and return freight remain part of the decision.
A fitted pair on file
Our first customers already own crates. They buy matched inserts and keep the approved geometry for the next tour.

slides.title: One tour opens the next
items: First shipment
A shipper nominates three repeat objects. We quote the molds, produce a trial pair and sit with the lead handler for fit approval.
Repeat booking
Each object receives a revision number. The shipper reorders by number before the next leg, with a fresh inspection on arrival.
Portfolio agreement
Once the shipper has ten active fits, we offer reserved production slots tied to its exhibition calendar.

slides.title: Two crafts under one roof
items: Ada Voss, collections handling
Ada leads contact-point reviews and signs off packing instructions with each registrar. Her team owns the record of every approved revision.
Mika Lane, biomaterials production
Mika runs mold tooling, drying schedules and lot inspection. The next hire will own environmental testing and the release checklist.

slides.title: The next three shipments
items: By month 4
Complete bench qualification for three vessel shapes. Document contact points, dimensional drift and impact response.
By month 9
Deliver paid trials to four shippers and track handling time, fit corrections and damage reports.
By month 15
Secure repeat orders from three shippers. Release a second mold set only after the first earns a repeat booking.

slides.title: Give the next tour a softer landing
items: $1.2M seed
$540k builds the mold and drying line. $360k funds qualification and handling trials. $300k funds shipper onboarding and repeat-order support.
The 15-month milestone is three paying repeat customers and one qualified production process. All venture details and figures in this pitch are fictional.
